findings.summary: Could not run the criterion 1–3 tests in the verifier snapshot because the shared build cache is stale. Those criteria rest on the recorded CI test pass.
findings.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core dispatch_writes_a_read_only_evidence_snapshot` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test status_snapshot` both failed with `Policy has no field named evidence` and `no method log_first_parent`, although the clean working tree contains those items. Cargo treated the base-built athena-agent and athena-git libraries as fresh. A forced rebuild via `cargo --config` was denied by policy, and I did not try to work around it. This is likely the fails-without revert build reusing artifact hashes in the same target dir; it is an Athena environment issue, not part of the candidate.

findings.summary: Files changed outside the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: None of the three is on the deliverables list. Each is a necessary follow-on change: job_plan.rs compares the prompt with the committed brief, which now differs by the placeholder; refusal_corpus.rs needs `evidence: None` to compile (it was in the planned files); shard-timings.txt registers the new status_snapshot test binary (a non-Rust data file).

findings.summary: The brief's `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot` hint only works when the target repository is Athena itself
findings.evidence: The section is added for every job that has a snapshot. For a repository without an athena-cli package the suggested command fails. A better approach would be to name the athena binary Athena already knows (HookSpec.athena_bin) or to state that the hint applies only to Athena's own repository. Read, Grep and Glob still work, so the snapshot remains usable.

findings.summary: The lock helpers duplicate existing code
findings.evidence: athena_git::snapshot already has the same chattr and write-bit walk (snapshot.rs:389-472), and unlock already uses it. Exposing a lock_dir there and adding the probe in core would avoid two copies that can drift apart.

findings.summary: The brief hard-codes '200' rather than deriving it from HISTORY_LIMIT
findings.evidence: athena-context cannot see athena_core::snapshot::HISTORY_LIMIT, so the two values can drift apart without any test noticing.

summary: The change does what the retry asked for. At dispatch it writes `<state>/jobs/<id>/evidence`, which holds `records/`, `landings/` (from the tree and the records branch) and `history.json` (the base commit and up to 200 first-parent commits, each with hash, commit time, subject and trailers). It removes write bits, sets chattr +i, then tries a write to confirm the lock holds; if any write succeeds, dispatch fails. Only the producer and verifier briefs get the snapshot path. Stored briefs use a `<state>` placeholder, and the prompts sent to agents use the real path. The agent policy lets those two roles read the directory, never write to it, and blocks escapes through `..`, symlinks or sibling directories with a similar name. `athena status --snapshot <dir>` works without a repository and uses the same record-assembly code (`Records::from_parts`) and the unchanged `Throughput::text`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-context` (109 passed), the athena-git `log_first_parent` test and the three athena-agent evidence policy tests; all passed. I could not build athena-core or athena-cli here: the shared target dir holds stale athena-agent/athena-git libraries built from base code, so the candidate's code fails with "no field `evidence`". My `--config` rebuild attempt was denied, so I did not work around it. Criteria 1–3 therefore rest on Athena's recorded CI `cargo test --locked` pass for this exact commit, plus my reading of the tests. Those tests drive the real `Athena::go` path, assert that create, append and remove are all refused, compare records byte for byte with the base commit, check the throughput text and include a check that the comparison is not vacuous. The remaining findings are minor: three changed files are not on the deliverables list (each needed to compile or keep tests consistent), the brief's `cargo run -p athena-cli` hint only works in Athena's own repo, and the chattr and write-bit helpers duplicate ones that already exist.
